rules.text: Public bind requires bearer token (generated+persisted 0600 if absent); loopback+no configured token is ungated; unresolvable token on public bind aborts startup (fail closed)
Token never printed or logged; constant-time compare; no ?token= query-param fallback on gated routes; token bootstrap via URL fragment only
Mutation routes refuse non-loopback peers unless --allow-remote-writes; shared-live deployment mode denies ALL writes regardless of peer
Non-loopback peer admitted via --allow-remote-writes is confined to project_root for fs writes; loopback keeps ADR-007 any-path breadth
Operation routes (/git/*, /skills, /search/content, /worktree/*) confined to default project_root or any registered non-archived project root; OUTSIDE_PROJECT_ROOT otherwise
Any path containing a .. component is rejected with PATH_TRAVERSAL on fs routes

Permission rendezvous: bounded timeout resolves deny; client disconnect denies its tickets after grace; first-response-wins; option_id re-validated against original options (TOCTOU); only session-subscribed clients may respond
Standalone server owns and kills its PTYs/agents on shutdown; desktop shared-live must never kill desktop agents; live PTY sessions survive project switches
Self-update is opt-in only (env or --check-update); signature verified before swap; never auto-restarts an unattended server
ACP install downloads archive, verifies sha256, extracts, atomically activates; request carries agentId only, host resolves everything from trusted catalog
WS clients authenticate in-protocol when gate active; event replay via cursors with per-session seq counters
Standalone owns its state roots (sessions, workspace-manifests, acp-catalog, acp-registry-binaries) exclusively; never shared with a desktop host on same machine
MCP OAuth flows: state/PKCE validated on callback; tokens stored atomically; pending flows bounded; expired tokens refreshed before deletion

findings.title: Dangling-symlink leaf escapes remote-write project_root confinement on /fs/write, /fs/copy, /fs/mkdir
findings.location: src-tauri/src/web/fs_api.rs:378-441 (resolve_request_path non-existent branch re-attaches leaf verbatim); callers fs_api.rs:560-578 (write), 889-918 (copy to), 517-543 (mkdir)
findings.repro: Remote peer admitted via --allow-remote-writes: ln -s /etc/cron.d/evil <project_root>/link (dangling). POST /fs/write {path: <project_root>/link} -> resolve_request_path returns <project_root>/link (inside, passes ensure_remote_within_project_root) -> fs::write follows the symlink and creates/writes /etc/cron.d/evil outside the boundary.
findings.evidence: path.exists() is false for a dangling symlink, so the ancestor-walk branch runs: parent canonicalizes inside project_root, leaf 'link' re-attached verbatim. Containment checks the unresolved leaf path, not the symlink target. fs::write/fs::copy/create_dir_all all follow the link.

findings.title: No Origin/Host validation on WS upgrades — drive-by DNS-rebinding RCE against ungated loopback standalone server (CWE-346)
findings.location: src-tauri/src/web/ws.rs ws_upgrade (no Origin check, no Host check); terminal_ws.rs:42-47 terminal_ws_upgrade; connect info passes 127.0.0.1 so check_local_only admits; router.rs PUBLIC_PATHS includes /ws and /terminal/ws
findings.repro: Attacker page (HTTP, or DNS-rebinding domain resolving to 127.0.0.1) opens ws://127.0.0.1:8080/terminal/ws on an ungated loopback termul-server: browser sends Origin: evil.com + Host: evil.com; server ignores both, peer is loopback -> PTY spawn = arbitrary command execution from a malicious web page. Same via /ws mutations and loopback-guarded HTTP routes (DNS rebinding: Host check absent).
findings.evidence: ws_upgrade/terminal_ws_upgrade read no headers; hyper sends Origin on WS handshakes; no PNA enforcement for ws:// to loopback from http pages. Standalone loopback default (no token, no gate) is the default install posture. Token-gated public binds resist (token required). Also CSWSH: token in localStorage never auto-sent on cross-site WS, so gated servers resist.

findings.title: /fs/read and ls/browse on special files: /dev/urandom OOM, /dev/zero, FIFO hang, block-device read — remote DoS via thread-pool exhaustion
findings.location: src-tauri/src/web/fs_api.rs:660-681 read uses fs::metadata len=0 for char devices then fs::read unbounded (/dev/urandom reads until OOM); /fs/info opens FIFO (blocking open); copy from FIFO blocks
findings.repro: GET /fs/read?path=/dev/urandom (token-authed remote peer) -> spawn_blocking thread reads until OOM. FIFO read hangs a blocking thread indefinitely; repeated requests exhaust the pool. ls on huge dirs -> unbounded response.
findings.evidence: Read routes are intentionally ungated for breadth (ADR-007) but authenticated remote clients can still exhaust the blocking pool. MAX_FILE_SIZE check uses metadata.len() which is 0 for procfs/devices before fs::read.

findings.title: GET /mcp-servers returns raw config incl env secrets; POST /mcp-servers/probe = unauthenticated arbitrary command spawn (shared-live deny-all-writes bypassed)
findings.location: src-tauri/src/web/mcp_servers_api.rs:24-61 get reads raw JSON incl command env; mcp_probe_api.rs:21-40 probe spawns Command from request body with no guard; remote/host.rs shared-live web_auth=None
findings.repro: On shared-live (cloudflared public tunnel, no token): GET /mcp-servers leaks MCP env secrets; POST /mcp-servers/probe {command:'sh -c ...'} spawns arbitrary commands on the host. On standalone 0.0.0.0 without token (operator error) same. With token, any authenticated client can probe (probe is by design a host-side exec).
findings.evidence: Shared-live passes web_auth None (mod.rs:206-209) so /mcp-servers* is reachable through the public tunnel; shared_live_writes_denied does not apply to probe (no check_local_only). Deferred-work and QA docs treat writes as denied on shared-live; probe + mcp-servers read violate that posture.

findings.title: question_request is durable (replayed to reconnecting clients) unlike permission_request — stale unanswerable questions
findings.location: src-tauri/src/acp/session_persistence.rs:1620-1636 is_durable_event excludes permission_request but NOT question_request
findings.repro: Agent asks a question; client answers + reconnects later with cursor replay: the stale question_request replays as an event even though the rendezvous ticket is gone; client shows an unanswerable question UI. Session payload fold ignores it in transcript but live replay delivers it.
findings.evidence: Issue #411 added question rendezvous; the durable-exclusion list was not updated. WsProtocol agent verified replay path delivers question_request on cursor replay and subscribe_snapshot.

findings.title: Ephemeral/live-only session transcript unrecoverable on reconnect (cursor subscribe returns Stale/NotFound)
findings.location: src-tauri/src/web/ws.rs handle_subscribe/subscribe_snapshot persistence-first path; session_persistence.rs flush_session SessionNotFound arm
findings.repro: Live ephemeral session with ring-buffer events: client reconnects and subscribes with cursor; persistence attached -> last_seq/flush return SessionNotFound -> reply Stale -> recovery dead-ends NotFound; transcript lost despite live ring events.
findings.evidence: WsProtocol verified the no-persistence replay branch is unreachable in server mode (persistence always attached on standalone + shared-live).

findings.title: dispatch_connection_text holds the per-connection lock across all handler awaits — head-of-line blocking delays respond_permission past the 60s rendezvous timeout
findings.location: src-tauri/src/web/ws.rs dispatch_connection_text (subscribed_clients lock held across handle_subscribe disk IO / install download awaits)
findings.repro: Client sends subscribe (disk-heavy replay) then respond_permission: the permission response queues behind the replay; slow installs/replays can push past DEFAULT_PERMISSION_TIMEOUT (60s) so an answered-in-time permission is denied.
findings.evidence: Static trace; needs a timing test to confirm real-world impact. send_prompt path bypasses the lock (accept_send_prompt outside).

findings.title: QuestionRendezvous denies on last-subscriber disconnect with NO grace period (permissions get 60s reconnect grace)
findings.location: src-tauri/src/web/permissions.rs QuestionRendezvous::with_timeout (no grace field) vs PermissionRendezvous DEFAULT_PERMISSION_RECONNECT_GRACE
findings.repro: Mobile client throttles + reconnects (5-15s per prod logs): a pending question is cancelled immediately on disconnect while a pending permission survives 60s.
findings.evidence: Inconsistent policy for the two rendezvous types; R-007 states bounded reconnect grace for pending tickets.

findings.title: WsRelaySink sessions map + SessionQueue + TurnWatermark grow unboundedly; forget_session never called on close_session
findings.location: src-tauri/src/web/sink.rs sessions map (only forget_session removes); permissions.rs SessionQueue empty entries; TurnWatermark maps
findings.repro: Create+close N sessions over a server's lifetime -> N retained event histories + queue/watermark entries; long-running VPS leaks memory proportional to session count.
findings.evidence: close_session does not call forget_session. Also enqueue send-failure removes client from clients/session_subs but not the connection's subscribed_clients list.

findings.title: handle_create_session/switch_project do not canonicalize/validate cwd — sessions spawnable in arbitrary or non-existent dirs
findings.location: src-tauri/src/web/ws.rs handle_create_session + handle_switch_project (cwd used verbatim; add_project path unvalidated on desktop-hosted mode)
findings.repro: WS create_session {cwd:'/nonexistent'} on standalone -> session created with cwd that does not exist; desktop-hosted mode accepts arbitrary paths (VPS mode validates via FileProjectRegistry).
findings.evidence: Divergent validation between deployment modes; sessions can be spawned outside any project boundary.

findings.title: Queued permission requests fanned out but unanswerable until promoted; promotion emits no signal; stale response errors
findings.location: src-tauri/src/web/permissions.rs SessionQueue promote_next (no event on promotion); relay fans out queued permission_request immediately
findings.repro: Two sessions' permissions queue: second is shown to the client; client responds -> 'stale' (ticket not yet promoted); promotion is silent; ticket later denied on timeout although the user answered.
findings.evidence: Queue promotion emits no projects_changed/permission event; clients see a dead request.

findings.title: install path performs NO sha256 verification despite docs claiming verify — MITM downgrade-redirect chain enables registry agent injection
findings.location: src-tauri/src/acp/install.rs:609-643 (no sha256 verification, comment says catalog trusted); web/mod.rs:105-110 + R-010 docs claim 'downloads + verifies (sha256)'; acp_registry_snapshot.rs follows https->http redirects with no size cap (deferred-work notes this)
findings.repro: Catalog fetch compromised (MITM or registry compromise): install downloads + activates attacker archive with zero integrity check. Snapshot fetch downgrade redirects are the pre-existing weak link.
findings.evidence: install.rs comment: 'No sha256 verification: the catalog is the trusted Zed ACP registry'; sha256 field is audit-only. Contradicts documented contract (R-010, mod.rs:105-110, router.rs:201-206). Fix is either verify when sha256 present or fix the docs.

findings.title: legacy acp_binary_install accepts untrusted archive URLs + same https->http downgrade; backup path collision can delete installed agents; EXDEV swap failure
findings.location: src-tauri/src/acp_binary_install.rs (archive URL from caller; backup path collision; /tmp staging rename across filesystems)
findings.repro: Desktop command path with crafted URL -> download from http after redirect; agent-id-shaped backup dirs can collide and remove installed agents; /tmp on separate fs -> install swap fails EXDEV.
findings.evidence: AcpServices agent verified each; legacy path retained for back-compat.

findings.title: mcp_oauth: pending_oauth_flows unbounded; store_token non-atomic; get_valid_token_blocking deletes expired tokens without refresh attempt; urlencode misses ?/#//; iss ignored
findings.location: src-tauri/src/acp/mcp_oauth.rs (token file write not atomic; blocking refresh path deletes expired; urlencode incomplete); web/mcp_oauth_api.rs pending flows map
findings.repro: Start N flows without completing -> map grows unbounded. Crash during token write -> corrupt token file. Expired token on blocking path is deleted instead of refreshed -> permanent loss. OAuth code containing #/? truncates the callback URL parse.
findings.evidence: AcpServices verified each hop; iss validation absent in oauth_callback.

findings.title: overlay_installed leaks absolute command paths to remote clients (contradicts catalog doc); catalog refresh CDN fetch unauthenticated
findings.location: src-tauri/src/web/catalog_api.rs:74-77 overlay_installed; :58 refresh param
findings.repro: GET /acp/catalog through public tunnel shows resolved absolute executable paths (host filesystem layout disclosure); ?refresh=true forces unauthenticated CDN fetch with multi-second delay (minor DoS).
findings.evidence: catalog_api.rs:46-50 says never carries resolved absolute executable paths; overlay does exactly that for installed agents.

findings.title: terminal_ws + PTY surface reachable without peer gating: shared-live tunnel clients spawn PTYs while shared_live_writes_denied claims ALL writes denied
findings.location: src-tauri/src/web/terminal_ws.rs:42-47 (no ConnectInfo/peer check; web_auth None on shared-live); remote/host.rs binds Localhost + cloudflared forwards public traffic as loopback
findings.repro: Any internet user with the shared-live tunnel URL opens /terminal/ws and spawns a shell: check_local_only routes are bypassed (peer appears loopback) AND terminal_ws itself has no gate. Terminal exec is a product feature via tunnel, but the deny-all-writes flag's documented promise is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: PtyTerminal agent: host::start always binds Localhost; tunnel makes remote clients appear loopback. Terminal-PTY-by-tunnel is intended product behavior (ungated URL is the barrier) — the defect is the documented invariant mismatch, not the feature.

findings.title: PtyManager kill/resolve issues: kill returns success for non-existent ids when hidden; kill spawn-blocking error skips cleanup; orphan reaper missing terminal_events.remove; resolve_shell_path does not search PATH on Unix
findings.location: src-tauri/src/pty/manager.rs kill (is_hidden check before lookup), cleanup paths, orphan reaper; resolve_shell_path fixed dirs only
findings.repro: kill(nonexistent) with app hidden -> Ok. Error-path kill skips resource cleanup. Reaper removes PTY but leaves tracker entries. User shell at ~/.local/bin/zsh not resolved (only fixed dirs searched).
findings.evidence: PtyTerminal agent verified each; low blast radius individually.

findings.title: update_orphan_detection timeout unit mismatch (ms vs secs) + idle forwarder generation checks + web attachment slot accounting leaks
findings.location: src-tauri/src/web/terminal_ws.rs:590-595 (timeout_ms logged); pty/manager.rs web_attachments accounting; claims.rs generation reset vs forwarder teardown gap
findings.repro: update_orphan_detection {timeout: 30000} treated as ms in one path and compared against secs elsewhere; web terminals never auto-unprotected -> slot exhaustion; claims issue() resets generation before forwarder teardown -> list_preserved reissues stale claims.
findings.evidence: PtyTerminal agent verified list_preserved/claims cluster; units mismatch verified by reading both call sites.

findings.title: Desktop and standalone share ~/.local/state/termul/store.json — web-store cross-contamination (SSH profiles, settings) between two products
findings.location: src-tauri/src/web/mod.rs:258-267 (store default under service_account_state_dir on both paths); desktop app-data isolation pattern used by other services
findings.repro: Run desktop + standalone on same machine: both open the same store.json; web client keys (SSH profiles, settings) collide and cross-contaminate.
findings.evidence: R-012 says state roots are never shared across processes/products; workspace-manifests/acp-catalog use isolated app_data_dir on desktop but store.json does not.

findings.title: RemoteServerState stop() does not disconnect live WS clients; can hang indefinitely on stuck in-flight request; bind_mode 'all' silently downgraded to localhost
findings.location: src-tauri/src/remote/host.rs stop() (axum on_upgrade detaches; no header read timeout); remote_server_start bind_mode param ignored
findings.repro: Toggle shared-live off while a client holds /ws: stop() returns, WS stays live until client disconnects. A wedged HTTP request (slowloris via tunnel) hangs graceful shutdown indefinitely. --bind all silently binds localhost.
findings.evidence: RemoteHost agent verified axum 0.8 detaches upgraded connections; hyper default lacks header read timeout.

findings.title: FsApi: delete on symlink-to-dir removes the TARGET tree (resolved path); rename moves target not link — desktop/web divergence and loopback data-loss footgun
findings.location: src-tauri/src/web/fs_api.rs:802-835 delete uses canonicalized path so a project symlink to a dir deletes the target recursively; rename :841-876 moves resolved target leaving link dangling
findings.repro: Loopback user deletes <project>/link (symlink to /data): remove_dir_all wipes /data. Desktop semantics remove only the link. Same for rename (moves /data, link dangles).
findings.evidence: resolve_request_path canonicalizes existing paths, so delete/rename operate on the target. Loopback keeps breadth (ADR-007) so this is a data-loss footgun rather than remote escape.

findings.title: FsApi: Windows rename replaces existing files + cross-volume moves (MOVEFILE_COPY_ALLOWED) — Unix EXDEV divergence; procfs size field inconsistent
findings.location: src-tauri/src/web/fs_api.rs rename/copy (std::fs::rename semantics differ by platform)
findings.repro: POST /fs/rename {to: existing-file} on Windows silently replaces; on Unix errors EEXIST/EXDEV. procfs files report size 0 with non-empty content.
findings.evidence: Rust std rename Windows flags; platform parity gap for the web client.

findings.title: Stale cross-drive boundary test contradicted CAP-2 registered-root semantics
findings.location: src-tauri/src/remote/host.rs:1227-1256 (fixed)
findings.repro: Baseline failure: test asserted dir_a rejected after default switch, but p-a stays registered+non-archived so CAP-2 admits it.
findings.evidence: Test predated PR #557 (ensure_within_project_boundary). Fixed by archiving p-a before the rejection assertion, preserving the test's boundary-moved intent.
